geo.name: Data Quality-Control
geo.det: Data quality control is important in the services being piloted because they are used within a Decision Support System (DSS). Data quality control will focus on making sure that services are running and information delivered is within expected values. Data quality indicators will provide information at the API service level.
geo.exc: The variable nature of the results provided through the APIs means that quality control at the file level is not feasible since it should not change if the services are running correctly.

geo.name: Data Preservation
geo.det: The API services are designed to bring EO information to software developers and therefore it is up to the customers to decide whether data should be preserved and how much they are willing to pay to preserve their data. Historical time series are envisioned as services but will not be expected to be preserved for the long term.

geo.name: Data Documentation
geo.det: Data are documented using ISO 19115 standard. Descriptive, Structural, and Administrative metadata are provided for each dataset.

geo.name: Data Traceability
geo.det: Datasets within GMP are created compiling data from various established monitoring networks. Each of them has different procedure of data acquisition and laboratory processing. Each record is tracable to its original monitoring network and data provider so the provenance information is provided.

geo.name: Data Quality-Control
geo.det: Data quality is controlled and evaluated during data acquisition at the level of individual monitoring networks. Each monitoring network has its own quality controll process. Data collected in GMP are based on data from monitoring networks. Furtheremore each Regional Organisation Group is responsible for data from its own region and does data review prior data and regional report publication. For the whole proces of GMP data collection campaign, there is a support of dedicated data manager who ensures smooth process of data collection to avoid data duplicates and other types of inconsistencies.

geo.name: Data Preservation
geo.det: GMP datasets are stored and operated within infrastructure of RECETOX, Masarik University. It provides long term commitment host GMP datasets and tools used to make data and matadata available. Data Seal of Approval is not currently applied.

geo.name: Data And Metadata Verification
geo.det:
1. Media refreshment is performed on daily basis performing periodic backups.
2. Data are archived in multiple formats - database dumps, simple CSV files with self contained description, backups of GIT repositories with wource code of related tools.
3. To avoid data loss we preserve data at 3 buildings, 2 geographic locations using 3 storage technologies (SSD, HDD, tape)
4. Systems and tools to make data available are operated in virtualised environment (single machine or cloud), HW is renewed every 3-7 years
5./6. Scheduled audits on readability and integrity of archived data are not done periodically but just randomly.
7. Primary data archive is database backup where integrity rules are applied

geo.name: Data Review And Reprocessing
geo.det: Data collected during GMP data collection campaign are managed by web application call GMP DWH Data Management Console (DMC). DMC force data providers to import data in batches which comes with basic description of purpose. In case a need of any change old import batch is cancelled and new one is introduced. After any change all datasets related to GMP are reprocessed. After GMP data collection campaigh is closed, changes in original data are rare and always needs an approval by Regional Organisational Group member.

geo.name: Online Access
geo.det: S1 retrieved winds are directly downloadable from the website as netcdf files for the actual data and png files for visualization purposes - after users are registered and logged in. User authentication implemented - follows DTU standards with SSO for DTU users. External users can create an account.

geo.name: Data Encoding
geo.det: Output data are available as netcdf files using standard format and attributes similar to the ones of input data from the original data producers, e.g. EUMETSAT, NOAA, etc. Mapping services used to disseminate the data on the website use OGC WMS standard https://www.ogc.org/standards/wms and Tiled Web Maps (OpenStreetMap standard)

geo.name: Data Documentation
geo.det: Input data are available and documented by the dedicated producing centers. Final output data that can be of direct interest to users are stored as netcdf files and partly documented according to metadata standards.

geo.name: Data Traceability
geo.det: Internal GitLab services, provided by DTU Wind Energy, are used for code maintainance and version tracking.

geo.name: Data Quality-Control
geo.det: Data produced by EUMETSAT and ESA are used to estimate the final products of the pilot and are already quality controlled through the agencies. The pilot products derived by the aforementioned data are filtered for appropriate flags relevant to the nature of the input data and are accompanied by sample size information. Validation excercises performed for assessing the data quality for the pilot's purposes have already been published in peer-review journals. We foresee at least 1 journal publication describing the data and services. Implementation of quality flags i SAR wind products is considered (i.e. flagging of bright targets, bathymetry, and non-neutral atm. stability conditions).

geo.name: Data Preservation
geo.det: Downloaded data from S1 and ASCAT are available online and also archived locally at DTU Wind Energy. Processed data are stored locally at DTU Wind Energy systems and back-up processes are in place.

geo.name: Data And Metadata Verification
geo.det: Input data and associated output data are achived locally at DTU Wind Energy using Tivoli Storage Management (TSM). The retrieval of archived data has been veriufied multiple times during sprint 2.

geo.name: Data Review And Reprocessing
geo.det: Data from EUMETSAT are occasionally reprocessed and when they become available they will be used instead of older products. Data from ESA are directly downloaded and processed internally at DTU Wind Energy, and can be occasionally re-processed to account for imporvements in atmospheric model inputs and inter-calibration between SAR sensors. Processes are in place interbnally to perform the reprocessing and that is not something final users can directly control or are influenced by. When updated products with different validation statistics to what was previously known become available, this will be disseminated through the website and through journal publications.

geo.name: Persistent And Resolvable Identifiers
geo.det: SAR wind retrievals performed at DTU Wind Energy will be assigned a DOI.

geo.name: Metadata For Discovery
geo.det:
DEIMS-SDR provides metadata following ISO19115/19139 implementing the eLTER community profile. This includes INSPIRE mandatory fields and are provided for the datasets shared in the pilot. Metadata are shared using pyCSW (following the OGC CSW) and OAI-PMH standard as well as providing a REST-API to access all metadata content as json documents.
Metadata are provided by the site managers and data providers. Basic quality checks only on the level of metadata completeness is conducted. Metadata content quality is checked by the metadata provider.
geo.exc: The DEMIS-SDR site metadata model is still revised periodically based on European and international requirements. Mappings of site metadata to ISO19115/19139 are done accordingly.

geo.name: Online Access
geo.det:
Data are shared using different repositories ranging from file based provision (e.g. B2SHARE, ZENODO) to service based provision using OGC SOS (e.g. eLTER Central Data Node). In addition locations of the long-term observation sites as well as spatial data are shared using OGC WFS/WMS provided by the eLTER Central Data Node.
The location of the data files is defined in the "online distribution link" defined in the metadata. The means of data sharing is subjected to the data providers.
geo.exc: Data could be due to embargo periods and restricted use (e.g. non-commercial). Data policy is defined on the level of the data providers.

geo.name: Data Encoding
geo.det:
File based in-situ data: different encodings for data could be used based on the communities. In general the eLTER Data Specification (following ICP IM) is recommended with a basic description of the data vocabulary. Biodiversity observation data are file based following different local taxonomies provided by the data providers.
Service based in-situ data: following the OGC SOS standard
Spatial data: mostly raster data shared as OGC WMS with SLD for data values
site locations: using OGC WFS/WMS providing centroid location and site identification (deims.id)
observation locations: using OGC WFS/WMS providing outline and identification of location (UUID)
Vocabulary: EnvThes is used as a common vocabulary to tag metadata (site and datasets) and enhance semantic interoperability

geo.name: Data Documentation
geo.det: Metadata are following ISO19115/19139 including elements of EML 2.0 on method description.

geo.name: Data Traceability
geo.det: Metadata on in-situ data are generated on demand when sharing the in-situ data and relevant information is provided. These data currently are in general not subjected to automated data pipelines.

geo.name: Data Quality-Control
geo.det: Data quality control procedures are subjected to the data providers and data quality control flags need to be implemented to the data as defined in the eLTER Data Specification for in-situ data. Work in the second sprint will evaluate options for quality control procedures within the mySITE pilot, if applicable.

geo.name: Data Preservation
geo.det:
B2SHARE is used as default repository for in-situ data if no secure data repository can be provided by the data providers. This ensures safeguarding and accessibility of the data and ensuring the longivety of the data.
DEIMS-SDR is used to collect information on the long-term observation sites. DEIMS-SDR is managed by the Umweltbundesamt GmbH and hosted at UK-CEH. It is included in the regular preservation procedures and backuped in regular intervals.
eLTER Central Data Node (CDN) is used to share in-situ data as OGC SOS service. eLTER CDN is hosted at UK-CEH and is included in the regular preservation services. Backups are done in regular intervals.

geo.name: Data And Metadata Verification
geo.det:
BSHARE: recommended data format for file based data is csv for data uploads to ensure long term usability. B2SHARE does not check for format transferability. 
EcoSense platform: is only caching metada in order to speed up visualisation. It is regulary renewed on a daily basis (during the night). 
DEIMS-SDR: Metadata of sites is verified using a publicly available QA tool (https://qa.deims.org/), datasets on DEIMS are validated using a dedicated, not publicly available ISO 19139 QA tool
eLTER Central Data Node (CDN) is continously updating the versions of geoserver (OGC WMS/WFS) and time series services (OGC SOS)

geo.name: Data Review And Reprocessing
geo.det: Data will be managed to perform corrections and updates in accordance with reviews, and to enable reprocessing as appropriate; where applicable this shall follow established and agreed procedures. Reviews are done by the data providers and updated versions are provided via B2SHARE (versioning). These procedures are currently defined for the emerging eLTER RI for participating long-term monitoring sites.
geo.exc: Data shared via the OGC SOS service of the eLTER CDN are not subject to versioning, as only the latest valid version of the data can be accessed. To overcome this limitation defined snapshots are planned to be shared. This will be implemented as follow up of the e-shape project.

geo.name: Persistent And Resolvable Identifiers
geo.det:
Persistent identification for long-term observation sites implemented with deims.id / DEIMS-SDR currently is not issuing PIDs/DOIs for MD records.
Persistent identification for in-situ data subjected to data providers, B2SHARE issues PID/DOI
geo.exc: eLTER Central Data Node (CDN) provides access to the latest version of valid data which raises the issue of dynamic data citation, which is not solved in the run time of the e-shape project.

Where possible code will be shared using gitHub (https://github.com/eLTER-RI/). This will be subject of the next implementations steps until 2023.

fair.q: Assess the interoperability of your data.
fair.det:
Workflows checking the interoperability of data (structural, semantic) are considered to be implemented (also part of the eLTER PLUS project as part of the eLTER RI implementation)
file-based in-situ data recommended eLTER Data Reporting format (following a line based and column based structure of data values)
service based in-situ data are structured following the recommendation of OGC SOS (O&M) using the reference implementation of 52°North.
site information follows the eLTER community standard for site documentation (Wohner in prep. 2022).
EnvThes vocabulary is used as common vocabulary to tag metadata and is continously extended to be used for data annotation following the recommendations of the RDA i-Adopt working group.

geo.name: Metadata For Discovery
geo.det: Our pilot has been working on the creation and publication of the Data and Metadata Standards for the Essential Biodiversity Variables we use in the Portal. These standards are currently based on NetCDF data structure standards and metadata standards provided by EML (XML) and ACDD (JSON) that make the portal data indexable by search engines.
geo.exc: Despite our efforts to integrate data without restrictions in some cases the EBV Data Portal includes data and services relevant for e-shape project users with some usage restrictions. This will be made clear in the license description of the EBV Data Portal catalog.

geo.name: Online Access
geo.det: To achieve data accessibility through online services we use a REST API. The data structure conforms to the open standards ACDD (JSON) and EML (XML).

geo.name: Data Encoding
geo.det: The standard to be used to structure the data is NetCDF (OGC).

geo.name: Data Documentation
geo.det: We are currently working to crosswalk the EBV standard with EML and ACDD terms. We plan to publish the standard and the results in a scientific paper.
geo.exc: Some terms and definitions in the proposed EBV standard used in the data portal are not defined in other standards.  The Ecological Metadata Language (EML) is a metadata specification specially developed for the discipline of ecology; it is the closest specification to EBVs, but it has been necessary to define for the first time some terms related to Essential Biodiversity Variables and their classification. We anticipate that the socialization of these new terms will be achieved through user communities and with the help of expert groups working on the subject, for which we have engaged the Biodiversity Information Standards (TDWG).

geo.name: Data Traceability
geo.det: The provenance of the information will be achieved through the specific fields that will be described in the EBVs' standard and that contain information about the origin and source of the information.
geo.exc: Due to the complexity of source information that may be associated with the Essential Biodiversity Variables we do not anticipate the possibility of visualizing this as part of the pilot.

geo.name: Data Quality-Control
geo.det: The data quality control process will be limited to two levels that will be facilitated by the Essential Biodiversity Variables Portal: first the adherence to the controlled vocabulary for defining metadata terms for EBVs, and second the visualization of these datasets in the EBV data portal. However, consideration will also be given to supporting the transmission of information between data publishers and users so that this feedback will assist in quality control.

geo.name: Data Preservation
geo.det: The Essential Biodiversity Variables Data Portal will adhere to the data loss prevention and remediation policies defined at the institutional level (DFG).In addition we will perform periodic self-assessment of GEOSS to evaluate our quality as a reliable digital repository (TDRs) and publish the results in the portal's website.

geo.name: Data And Metadata Verification
geo.det: The Essential Biodiversity Variables Data Portal will adhere to the data loss prevention and remediation policies defined at the institutional level (DFG) with a co-located copy of the original data and an off-site copy. In addition, we will ensure that data transfers are error-free by verifying the integrity of the files at source and destination.

geo.name: Data Review And Reprocessing
geo.det: In a dynamic balance between resources available to curate data and resources to include more data in the EBVs Data Portal, automated mechanisms will be created to invite authors to update their data. In the event that they respond with updates and collections, resources will be prioritized by defining priorities based on data usage by the community.

geo.name: Persistent And Resolvable Identifiers
geo.det: At the moment the EBV standard and the portal only allow for the utilization of DOIs for the published scientific articles that support the data, but not the actual event of uploading and making the data available on the portal.

fair.det: Our pilot is working on the creation and publication of the Data and Metadata Standards for the Essential Biodiversity Variables that we will use in the Portal. These standards are based on the NetCDF data structure standards and the metadata standards provided by EML (XML) and ACDD (JSON) that will make the portal data searchable by search engines.

fair.q: Outline the identifiability of data and refer to standard identification mechanism.
fair.det: At the moment the EBV standard and the portal only allow for the utilization of DOIs for the published scientific articles that support the data, but not the actual event of uploading and making the data available on the portal.

fair.q: Outline naming conventions used
fair.det: EML and ACDD

fair.q: Outline the approach towards search keyword
fair.det: Within the EBV Data Portal we have created a database that contains all the metadata of the existing information in the portal, this information is indexed and it is possible to search it using keywords. In the future we will refine this internal search engine.

fair.q: Outline the approach for clear versioning
fair.det: Data versioning has been implemented in the portal on an initial basis, and it is planned to refine this process as a next step.

fair.q: Specify standards for metadata creation (if any).
fair.det: We have been working on the implementation of an Essential Biodiversity Variables (EBSV) data and metadata standard. This process should be refined and the Standard should be published.

fair.q: Specify which data will be made openly available?
fair.det: Our goal is to make all the data that are archived in the Essential Biodiversity Variables Portal will be made openly available. In the event that there are embargoes of information due to publication processes, they will be taken into account.

fair.q: Specify how the data will be made available
fair.det: The data will be made available through web-based data portal (EBV Data Portal) that will allow users to freely download all information including data and metadata. A data service will also be created through a REST API that will allow the consumption of this service and its information products by other initiatives of the consortium and also external services.

fair.q: Specify what methods or software tools are needed to access the data?
fair.det: The NetCDF format that will be used to share the data is a widely adopted and well-established format used in the scientific communities specially the climate community and therefore benefits from many open access tools that allow its handling, analysis and visualization. We will provide a directory of the most common ones in the EBV Data Portal. However, in the spirit of facilitating accessibility we will also provide an R library that allows the conversion of NetCDF data to a variety of common geospatial formats (e.g., GeoTIFF, ASCII, etc.).

fair.q: Specify where the data and associated metadata, documentation and code are deposited
fair.det: The EBVs data and metadata will be archived and documented in the database associated with the EBV Data Portal.

fair.q: Specify how access will be provided in case there are any restrictions
Assess the interoperability of your data.
fair.det: The NetCDF format a widely adopted and well-established data format will be used for the data. For the metadata we will propose a new standard for the EBVs that will be made available in Ecological Metadata Language EML (XML) and the Attribute Convention for Data Discovery ACDD (JSON)used in the scientific communities.

fair.q: Specify whether you will be using standard vocabulary for all data types present in your data set, to allow inter-disciplinary interoperability?
fair.det: We plan to use the standard vocabulary terms from Ecological Metadata Language EML (XML).

fair.det: The objective of our pilot is not to create data di novo but rather to serve as an information broker for disconnected groups by providing the service of archiving and documenting data through a data and metadata standard. Therefore, data licensing and usage restrictions will be determined by the data providers.

geo.det:
The eshape deliverable (i.e. a European record of Sentinel-1 derived flood extent maps) will be generated as part of the new Global Flood Mapping component of the Copernicus Emergency Managament Service. A requirement of CEMS is that API Endpoints will be developed according to RESTful standards. CEMS requires that the proposed data access and dissemination system is designed under the proposition to follow four fundamental goals in accessing the product access system. Access to the actively maintained metadata base is given via the well-defined OGC CSW standard referred to as metadata catalogue 
• easy to use and yet highly powerful access and dissemination methods, 
• high availability with state-of-the-art failover scenarios, 
• mature scale-out in terms of load to serve when needed in time and 
• fully integrable in existing solutions like the CEMS platform by applying open and flexible technology stacks.

geo.det: Our partners from Geoville are responsible for the online access to the CEMS database. According to them the development of the dissemination system will be done in an agile software development process, to ensure high quality and delivery in time. geo.det: Sentinel-1 GRD scenes are downloaded to EODC followed by quality checks and the ingestion of the corresponding metadata data into the operated metadata infrastructure. In the pre-processing of the Sentinel-1 GRD data takes place. Metadata records are produced and inserted into the metadata database upon completion of the pre-processing task. The third part of the workflow relates to the actual generation of the flood product. The flood product is stored in the Sentinel-1 20m flood datacube with metadata written to the metadata infrastructure.

geo.name: Data Review And Reprocessing
geo.det: Regular data reprocessing is planned as part of the operational Global Flood Monitoring Service. We will continuously evaluate the possibility to evolve the flood production system, as several algorithmic enhancements are expected to be available for implementation in the coming years. This includes enhanced methods for flood detection, uncertainty estimation, and exclusion masking, the extended attribution of local meteorological conditions, as well as system enhancements leading to improved usability and spatio-temporal coverage, anticipating an increase in capacity and timeliness of measurements of the Sentinel-1 mission (e.g. by the addition of the Sentinel-1C sensor). A reprocessing workflow will be optimised for High Performance Computing through parallelisation and most direct interfaces to the Sentinel-1 data cube. This will allow us to perform requested reprocessing tasks of the global GFM product archive, aiming for a comprehensive, consistent, and harmonised product.

geo.det: The service and output products will all be exposed in the NextGEOSS Catalogue by June 2022. Automatic user authentication and authorization by SSO shall be enabled in the web geoportal.

geo.name: Data Encoding
geo.det: Data products of the pilot are generated in geotiff and shapefile, depending on the product. In terms of content, the only vocabulary that we are aware of for the fisheries management thematic fields is the Reference Tables Management System being developed by FAO within the Fisheries Global Information System (FIGIS) (https://www.fao.org/fishery/en/topic/18046/en). The pilot team will do an effort to adapt the pilot products to follow this vocabulary.

geo.name: Data Documentation
geo.det: A metadata .xml file was created for each of the products generated by the pilot. These were populated according to the ISO19115 standard. Besides mandatory fields, additional fields were included, as recommended by GEO in this data management plan.

geo.name: Data Traceability
geo.det: Metadata files for all products include information on provenance data, but not on processing steps. The pilot team shall document processing steps after June 2022, adding references to algorithms and versions. The products metadata can be updated in an automatized manner.

geo.name: Data Quality-Control
geo.det: Data products are being internally reviewed for quality, in the mean while in the metadata’s data quality field only a description on the products lineage is considered. Nevertheless, there was a concern on the quality assurance of the data, from the provenance data and across the processing steps. For example, in terms of preparation of AIS data for processing, for completeness, points with a low emission rate were not considered and, for accuracy, velocities higher than 30 knots were removed; in terms of preparation of e-logbooks captures data, fishing events with wrong datetime or coordinates were flagged and removed.

fair.q: Assess the interoperability of your data.
fair.det:
GEO-DAMP already facilitates the access to heterogeneous data, including EO, climate and other collateral sources using different standards, e.g.: GEO-DAMP Discovery services (OpenSearch), GEO-DAMP Access services (REST Web Services), GEO-DAMP Processing services (REST Web Services). MEEO ADAM platform currently exposes standardised OGC services for data discovery, visualization, access and processing, to facilitate the integration of ADAM resources within user’s stacks. WMS is available to users who want to quickly visualize data collections within their clients. An OpenSearch catalogue service (CSW) is exposed to discover all data within the platform through the various data facilities. The connection to INSPIRE compliant catalogues is also supported. The WCS is the core part of the DAS module. WCS can be queried directly via REST queries. Most of the processing capabilities can be triggered through WPS calls. Finally, serialisation formats (e.g. NetCDF, XML, JSON) are supported by standard schemas and conventions and the use of open standards.

geo.name: Online Access
geo.det: The maps and graphs will be accessible via online servcies: sub-seasoanl forecast service on Ilmanet platform,  seasonal forecast service on sesoanl.fmi.fi portal and and http://unesco-weather.gr, direct download

geo.exc: no exception

geo.exc: no exception

geo.name: Data Traceability
geo.det: No metadata creation. The algorithms used for the post-processing of sub-seasonal and seasonal forecast model data and production of forecasts outputs will be documented and made available on GitHub.
geo.exc: no exceptions

geo.name: Data Quality-Control
geo.det: ECMWF EPS data and seasonal data from C3S  undergo a checking routine for correct metadata and physical plausibility. The input forecast data is quality controlled, quality assessment of the forecasts using re-forecasts will be provided.
geo.exc: no exception

geo.name: Data Preservation
geo.det: The generated maps and graphs are planned to be archived partly on the pilot developers' (FMI and AoA) infrastructure, partly on DIAS platform. The archived FMI forecast products (data and visualized maps) will be stored for a max of two years.
geo.exc: no exceptions

geo.name: Data And Metadata Verification
geo.det: Implemented in the services technical infrastructure, production flow is periodically verified.
geo.exc: no exceptions

geo.name: Data Review And Reprocessing
geo.det: The service infrastructure and runs are checked and corrections are made whenever errors occur during the forecast runs.
geo.exc: Reprocessing: time and resources constrains
